About Us

The Nirmaan Philosophy

Create. Converse.
Change.

Nirmaan is not just a name. It is a statement — that something is being built, deliberately, unapologetically, and with purpose. As the Indraja Foundation's debut conference, Nirmaan is where vision takes form, where ideas are not just discussed but constructed, challenged, and redefined.

At Nirmaan, diplomacy is not performative. Debate is not mechanical. And participation is not passive. Every room demands substance. Every voice carries weight. Every moment is designed to push you beyond the expected.

This conference stands on the belief that youth are not waiting for change — they are creating it. Backed by a relentless team, a sharp Executive Board, and agendas that demand more than surface-level understanding, Nirmaan promises an experience that is intense, transformative, and impossible to forget.

Secretariat & Speakers

A Message from the Founder

"Nirmaan is… a little personal to me. It comes from this constant feeling that we're capable of so much more than what we're usually given space for. And at some point, I just decided — why not create that space? I'm not looking for perfect speeches or textbook diplomacy here. I'm looking for real thoughts, strong opinions, and people who aren't afraid to stand by them. Come a little curious, a little bold, maybe even a little rebellious. Because honestly? That's where the best conversations begin."

— Kavya Nidhi

Founder, Nirmaan MUN & Indraja Foundation

MUN Glossary

Moderated Caucus

A form of debate where delegates are called upon by the Chair to speak for a set amount of time on a specific sub-topic.

Unmoderated Caucus

Informal debate time where delegates can freely move around the room to discuss and draft resolutions.

Working Paper

A rough draft of ideas and solutions compiled by a group of delegates before forming a formal Draft Resolution.

Draft Resolution

A document written in resolution format, approved by the chairs, and introduced to committee but not yet voted upon.

Operative Clause

The part of a resolution which describes how the UN will do something about a certain issue. It begins with an action verb.

Preambulatory Clause

The part of a resolution that describes previous actions taken on the topic and reasons why the resolution is necessary.

Point of Order

A point raised when a delegate believes the chair or another delegate has made an error in the rules of procedure.

Point of Information

A question directed to the delegate speaking or to the chair, typically regarding the contents of a speech.

Placard

A piece of cardstock with a country's name on it that a delegate raises in the air to signal to the chair that they wish to speak.

Quorum

The minimum number of delegates who must be present for a committee to conduct business.

Bloc

A group of countries in a similar geographical region or with a similar opinion on a particular topic.

Veto Power

The ability, held by China, France, the Russian Federation, the UK, and the USA to prevent any draft resolution in the Security Council from passing.

Communiqué

A brief report or statement released by a committee, typically the crisis committee, regarding actions they have taken.

Dais

The group of people, usually high school or college students, in charge of a MUN committee.

Yielding the Floor

When a delegate finishes their speech and gives their remaining time back to the Chair or to another delegate.

Right of Reply

A right to speak in reply to a previous speaker's comment, invoked when a delegate feels their country's national integrity has been insulted.

Sanctions

Actions taken by countries against others for political reasons, either unilaterally or multilaterally.

Consensus

A group agreement achieved without formal voting, where no delegate actively objects to the passing of the motion.
